g.text: Rendered evidence from captured output

diagnostics, tool calls, prompt rendering, and asynchronous eval runs.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **The MCPJam API is in preview.** It
works today and we use it ourselves, but\n> it has not been generally announced and the surface may change — including in\n> break
ing ways — while we finish the design. Pin your integration to the\n> behaviors documented on this page, build a [tolerant\n> read
er](#versioning--stability), and expect to revisit it. Feedback is very\n> welcome on [Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) or\
n> [GitHub](https://github.com/MCPJam/inspector/issues).\n\n> [card] [Create an API key](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)

>
> Go straight to key management in the hosted app. If you're signed out,
> you'll be asked to sign in and then land right ba

ck on the API keys page.

The MCPJam API lets you operate the MCP servers saved in your
[hosted](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted

/overview.md) projects — from CI, scripts, or your own agents —
without opening the UI.

What you can do with it today:

* **
Discover your resources** — list your projects, their servers, eval\n suites, and chat sessions, so every ID the other routes nee

d is
 self-serve
* **Validate a server** — connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot
* **Run the doctor** — the p
robe → connect → initialize → capabilities workflow\n* **Check OAuth requirements** — does this server need an OAuth grant?\n* **L
ist tools, prompts, and resources** — the server's MCP primitives\n* **Call a tool / render a prompt** — execute primitives and ge
t the MCP result back verbatim\n* **Read a resource** by URI\n* **Export a full snapshot** — tools, resources, and prompts as one
JSON document\n* **Manage a project's clients** — list, read, **create** (from a built-in\n template like `claude`/`chatgpt`/`cur
sor`, or from a full config), edit,\n duplicate, and delete the named, reusable configurations that define how\n MCPJam connects
to and talks to your MCP servers. Edits are compare-and-set:\n read the client, then send its `configId` back as `expectedConfig
Id` for a\n config change and its `name` back as `expectedName` for a rename — a rename\n does not rotate the config, so the con
fig token cannot detect a concurrent\n one — and a concurrent edit is rejected rather than silently reverted\n* **Manage a projec
t's environments** — list, read, create, edit, archive, and\n restore the named execution bundles (host + optional server group +
optional\n pinned skills and plugin versions) that eval suites and goals run against,\n and **preview** what one resolves to be
fore launching it\n* **List a project's studies** — name, access mode, attached servers, and\n share link — and **read one study'
s settings**: model, system prompt,\n tool-approval policy, and resolved servers\n* **Author eval suites** — create a runnable su
ite (name, default model, servers, test cases) synchronously and get a `suiteId` back; no run is started and no credits are spent\
n* **Run eval suites asynchronously** — create a run from a saved suite, get a `202` + `runId`\n immediately, then poll status, p
er-iteration results (tool calls, token\n usage, latency), and full traces. Runs appear live in the hosted UI,\n tagged `source:
\"api\"`\n* **Manage a server's accounts** — complete OAuth yourself (e.g. the SDK's\n `runOAuthLogin`, or your CI's own sign-in
) and upload the token to a named\n account; list, rename, choose the default, and delete accounts. Tokens are\n write-only: no
route returns one\n* **Run a headless agent turn** — send a message history, get back the\n assistant reply, the platform operati
ons it invoked, references to any\n resources it created (eval suites), and token usage; the model is pinned\n server-side and b
illed to the project\n* **Send feedback** — report a bug, a missing capability, or something\n confusing to the MCPJam team at th

e moment you hit it; the same endpoint the
 `send_feedback` MCP tool calls

All endpoints operate on servers you have already

added to a project in the
hosted inspector. Managing API keys remains UI-only — see
[Not in the API yet](#not-in-the-api-yet).

## Base URL

```text theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1
```

The API is path-versioned. All

routes on this page are relative to the base
URL above.

## Authentication

Every request needs an MCPJam API key in the `Au

thorization` header:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -X POST \
 "https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$
PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/tools\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json

" \
 -d '{}'
```

### Creating a key

1. Open [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)
 in
the hosted app (the card at the top of this page takes you there\n directly).\n2. Click **Create API key**, name it, and pick th
e **organization** it will act in.\n3. Copy the key (`sk_…`) immediately — **it is shown exactly once** and never\n stored by MC

PJam in retrievable form.

Keys can be revoked from the same page at any time. Revocation takes effect
immediately.

### Scop

e

A key is bound to one MCPJam organization at creation and acts **as you,
inside that organization**. Per-request authorizati
on still applies: a call\nonly succeeds if the key's owner can access that project and server. A key\ncan never reach projects out

side its organization.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Two deliberate restrictions while in preview:
>
> * **API keys cannot manage API keys.
** Requests to the key-management surface\n> with an `sk_…` bearer fail with `403 FORBIDDEN`. Create and revoke keys in\n> the

UI.
> * **Guest sessions cannot use the API.** Sign in to create keys.

### Keep keys secret

Treat an API key like a passwo

rd:

* Load it from an environment variable or secret manager — never commit it to
 source control or ship it in client-side c
ode.\n* Scope keys narrowly: one key per integration, named so you can tell them apart.\n* Rotate by creating a replacement key, s
witching traffic, then revoking the old one.\n* If a key leaks, revoke it immediately in\n [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.

mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

If you see `401 UNAUTHORIZED` with `details.reason: "ORPHANED_KEY"`, the key
is no longer bou

nd to an organization and cannot be used — create a new key
from [Settings](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

## Conv

entions

**Requests.** Operations on servers are `POST` with a JSON body (most accept
an empty `{}`). **Reads** — the catalog l

istings and eval-run polling — are
`GET` and take their options (`cursor`, `limit`, filters) as query
parameters.

**Responses

.** Three envelope shapes, used consistently:

| Kind | Shape |
| - | - |
- [MCPJam Docs](https://docs.mcpjam.com/index.md): T
est, debug, and evaluate MCP servers, MCP apps, and ChatGPT apps across every major AI client.\n- [MCPJam in Claude](https://docs.
mcpjam.com/hosted/claude-connector.md): Connect Claude to your MCPJam account through the hosted MCP server — projects, saved serv
ers, evals, and user testing\n- [GitHub Checks](https://docs.mcpjam.com/github-checks.md): Run an eval suite against the MCP serve
r built from every pull request, and read the result as a check run, a pull-request comment, and a machine-readable JSON block.\n-
[Host Compatibility](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/host-compat.md): See which hosts your MCP server will work in — Claude, Ch
atGPT, Cursor, Copilot, Codex Desktop — the moment you connect\n- [Playground](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/playground.md): C
hat with your MCP servers, invoke tools by hand, render widgets, and inspect every step — all in one IDE-style workspace\n- [Evalu
ate](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/evals.md): Author test cases for your MCP server, run them across models, and gate pass/fai
l on deterministic assertions plus optional LLM-as-judge.\n- [My First ChatGPT App](https://docs.mcpjam.com/guides/first-chatgpt-a
pp-react.md): Build a simple Coffee Shop ChatGPT App with React\n- [Local Evals](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/local-evals.md): Run
an MCPJam eval suite file on your machine with mcpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity\n- [MCP Events](https://docs.
mcpjam.com/cli/events.md): List, poll, watch, subscribe to and conformance-check MCP Events (triggers) from the CLI: push, poll an
